evals.prompt: I need daily rainfall and max/min temperature for Honduras for 2020 and 2021. Save it to D:/data/hnd_climate. I don't have any API keys set up.
evals.expected_output: The skill routes pr to CHIRPS and tasmax/tasmin to CHIRTS, resolves Honduras to a bbox, shows a routing plan, and on confirmation writes a lowercase-key aggeodata YAML and calls run_download. The config must set general.use_zarr: true (the Zarr archives need no credentials and are far faster than one file per day), download_format: zarr, output_format: zarr with zarr_codec: zstd, and ncores: 4 — the one-worker cap belongs to data.chc.ucsb.edu, and with use_zarr nothing reaches it. No AgERA5 variable should appear in the plan, because the user said they have no keys and AgERA5 is the only source that needs one.

assertions.name: routes_pr_to_chirps_and_temp_to_chirts
assertions.description: climate.variables has pr: {source: chirps} and tasmax/tasmin: {source: chirts}

assertions.name: zarr_backend_enabled
assertions.description: general.use_zarr is true, and each chirps/chirts variable either inherits it or sets use_zarr: true

assertions.name: yearly_zarr_download_layout
assertions.description: general.download_format is "zarr", so each year lands as one store per variable rather than one file per day

assertions.name: zarr_cube_output_with_zstd
assertions.description: general.output_format is "zarr" and general.zarr_codec is "zstd" — blosc cannot be read by GDAL/QGIS

assertions.name: ncores_is_four_not_one
assertions.description: general.ncores is 4. Setting 1 means the skill applied the UCSB connection cap to a plan that never touches UCSB

assertions.name: no_agera5_without_a_key
assertions.description: No variable is routed to agera5, since the user stated they have no API keys

assertions.name: config_uses_lowercase_section_keys
assertions.description: The YAML uses dates / spatial_info / climate / soil / general / paths, not the legacy UPPERCASE aliases

assertions.name: plan_shown_before_downloading
assertions.description: A routing plan naming the variables, sources, period and bbox is shown and confirmed before run_download is called

evals.prompt: can you get me precipitation + solar radiation for just the Yoro department in Honduras, 2019-2021? no CDS account here. output to /data/yoro
evals.expected_output: The skill confirms the admin unit spelling with list_admin_units before resolving Yoro to a bbox, rather than guessing a name the boundary file may not use. pr routes to CHIRPS; rsds routes to NASA POWER rather than AgERA5, because the user has no CDS key, and the skill says so and notes NASA POWER is 0.5 degree so radiation is near-uniform over a department. The config sets use_zarr: true for pr only — setting it on a nasa_power variable is a validation error, not a no-op — and general.nasa_power_backend: s3.

assertions.name: admin_unit_spelling_confirmed
assertions.description: list_admin_units (or the equivalent) is consulted for Honduras before a feature name is passed to the extent resolver

assertions.name: rsds_falls_back_to_nasa_power
assertions.description: rsds is routed to nasa_power, not agera5, and the substitution is explained to the user

assertions.name: use_zarr_not_set_on_nasa_power
assertions.description: The nasa_power variable carries no use_zarr key — the schema rejects it for sources without a Zarr archive

assertions.name: resolution_tradeoff_stated
assertions.description: The reply notes NASA POWER's 0.5 degree cell is coarse relative to a single department

assertions.name: sub_country_extent_used
assertions.description: The extent is the Yoro bbox, not the whole of Honduras

evals.prompt: I already pulled CHIRPS for Malawi from the UCSB servers last year and the files are in /data/mwi/pr_raw. I want to extend that series through 2023 — same variable, same area.
evals.expected_output: This is the case where the Zarr default is wrong and the skill must say so. The mirror serves CHIRPS v3 (station-blended) while the package's UCSB endpoint serves CHIRP v3 (satellite-only) — different products — and server-side clipping can leave an edge pixel the Zarr slice drops, so the per-day grids differ. The skill should set use_zarr: false for this run, set ncores: 1 because the request now goes to data.chc.ucsb.edu, explain both reasons, and not silently extend the series with a different product.

assertions.name: use_zarr_disabled_for_continuation
assertions.description: use_zarr is false for the chirps variable rather than inheriting the skill's default

assertions.name: product_difference_explained
assertions.description: The reply states that the mirror and the UCSB endpoint serve different precipitation products, so mixing them within one series is not safe

assertions.name: ncores_returns_to_one
assertions.description: general.ncores is 1, because the per-file backend reinstates the UCSB connection cap

assertions.name: does_not_silently_use_the_default
assertions.description: The skill does not simply apply use_zarr: true and proceed without raising the mismatch

evals.prompt: download pr, tasmax, tasmin and rsds for bbox [-87.8, 14.0, -86.8, 15.0] for 2021, I'll be feeding the result into a crop model so I need a netcdf
evals.expected_output: The bbox is passed straight through without geocoding. The user named a NetCDF requirement, so output_format becomes "both" (or "netcdf") and the skill says why — the default Zarr store is not what they asked for. Everything else keeps the defaults: use_zarr: true, download_format: zarr, ncores: 4. The skill should not interrogate the user about what the cube is for, and should not need to name any particular downstream tool; the user already stated the requirement.

assertions.name: bbox_passed_through_unchanged
assertions.description: spatial_info.extent is the supplied bbox; no country or admin lookup is performed

assertions.name: netcdf_requirement_honoured
assertions.description: general.output_format is "both" or "netcdf", not the "zarr" default

assertions.name: download_layout_still_zarr
assertions.description: general.download_format stays "zarr" — the NetCDF request is about the stacked cube, not the files on disk

assertions.name: fetch_backend_still_zarr
assertions.description: general.use_zarr stays true — the NetCDF request says nothing about how the data is fetched

assertions.name: no_unnecessary_questioning
assertions.description: The skill acts on the stated requirement rather than asking the user what the cube is for
